payout_quote: For all other elections, Judges and Alternate Judges will receive $20.00 per hour and clerks will receive $17.00 per hour.
steps: Complete the Fort Bend County Poll Worker Application and e-mail it to vote@fortbendcountytx.gov, mail it to Elections Department/Poll Workers, 301 Jackson Street, Richmond, Texas 77469, or fax it to 281-341-4418.
Attend the paid Election Law Class (2 to 2.5 hours, held two days prior to an election); judges and alternate judges must attend, and all poll workers must attend before a primary election.
Arrive at the polling place at 6:00 AM on Election Day and remain until the polls are closed and results are called in or transported to Election Central.
Sign in at the front desk with the last four digits of your Social Security number so the Elections Office can calculate pay for the Election Day payroll.
Expect the check 4 to 6 weeks after the election.
catches: County-stated rates apply to non-primary elections only; for a primary election, pay is determined by the Secretary of State for the State of Texas.
Pay is hourly, so the total depends on hours actually worked — the county states only the hourly rate, not a fixed per-election total.
Class pay is only paid if you work the election (defined as working a minimum of 4 hours in the upcoming election); attend but do not work and the class is unpaid.
Checks arrive 4 to 6 weeks after the election, and 'it could be longer due to missing poll worker information.'
biggest_catch: $20/hr judges and alternate judges / $17/hr clerks applies only to non-primary elections; primary-election pay is set by the TX Secretary of State. It is an hourly rate for a full-day commitment starting at 6:00 AM and ending only after close and results transport, with the check arriving 4-6 weeks later.
eligibility: County page publishes an open application to all types of workers; bilingual (especially Spanish) workers are sought. The page does not publish citizenship, age, or voter-registration requirements; training attendance rules apply to judges, alternates, and (for primaries) all workers.
timing: Arrive at the polling place at 6:00 AM on Election Day; polling places open 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM; workers must remain until the polls are closed and results are called in or transported to Election Central. Early voting hours vary from election to election.
weasel_words: You should get your check in 4 to 6 weeks after the election

c1.evidence: Fort Bend County's own official 'Become an Election Worker' page publishes poll-worker compensation.

c2.evidence: Concrete amounts: Judges and Alternate Judges $20.00 per hour, clerks $17.00 per hour (non-primary elections); training class paid based on time spent in class.

c3.evidence: Official work hours: arrive 6:00 AM on election days; polls open 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM; must remain until polls close and results are called in or transported to Election Central.

c4.evidence: Page is live on fortbendcountytx.gov with applications now being accepted; rates stated in present tense on the county's active recruitment page.

s1.note: Hourly rates are exact: $20.00/hr judges/alternates, $17.00/hr clerks.

s2.note: Hours explicit with open-ended close: 6:00 AM arrival, 7:00 AM-7:00 PM voting, remain until close and results transport.

s3.note: Application path explicit: Poll Worker Application via email, mail, or fax; training is paid and scheduled by the county.

s4.note: No mileage or meal reimbursement stated — treated as not published.

s5.note: Hourly rate means totals vary with hours worked; class pay requires working a minimum of 4 hours in the election — caveats noted.

s6.note: Open to all types of workers; bilingual (especially Spanish) sought; the page does not publish citizenship/age/registration requirements, so none are asserted.

s7.note: No fees or cost barriers identified.

notes: Fort Bend County, Texas election workers. Current county-published rates for non-primary elections: $20.00/hr judges and alternate judges, $17.00/hr clerks; primary-election pay is set by the TX Secretary of State. Work day: 6:00 AM arrival, 7:00 AM-7:00 PM voting, remain until close and results called in/transported. Training (2-2.5 hr class, two days prior) is paid if the worker works the election.
payout_value_note: Hourly rate; total depends on hours worked. $17/hr clerks, $20/hr judges and alternate judges for non-primary elections; primary-election pay set by the TX Secretary of State.
numeric_basis: 6:00 A.M. arrival through 7:00 P.M. poll close = 780 minutes minimum; workers must remain until polls close and results are called in or transported to Election Central, so the actual day can run longer — end time is open-ended.
